change_summary: Static (frozen entry) stop vs ATR-trailing stop, canonical 3 windows on current code; static is the EV-optimal policy.
changed_variable: Stop exit policy: static frozen entry-stop (resting GTC STOP, set once) vs daily trailing stop (high-water-mark * (1 - TRAILING_STOP_PCT)). Pick the EV-maximizing one and make backtester + live execution share it.
hypothesis: A static/frozen protective stop set once at entry (resting GTC STOP) maximizes EV over a daily-trailing stop on the canonical 3 windows; align backtester and production to the winner, closing the stop-policy parity gap that the bracket-order playbook now makes executable.
notes: Static stop = documented baseline (EV 7.8941, reproduced bit-exact). ATR trailing loses in all 3 windows: trail(3,2) 5.5377 (-2.36 EV / -30% / -101k), trail(4,2) 3.4325 (-57%). Worst-DD ~same (~11%), so trailing buys no risk reduction - it cuts winners short before the 3.5xATR target. Confirms exp-20260503-009 (which rejected trailing on the old 5.18 baseline). DECISION: static wins; backtester already aligned (uses static). Production/operator action: set the protective stop ONCE at entry and do NOT trail it up; the bracket-order playbook stop leg should emit the static entry stop, not open_positions trailed stop_price. Added a default-off --set CONFIG override to backtester.py (baseline bit-exact).

post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not re-run ATR-trailing-stop sweeps (TRAIL_TRIGGER/OFFSET) on these 3 windows - now confirmed twice (this + exp-20260503-009) that static dominates. Do not retune trail trigger/offset hoping for a win.
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: Only revisit trailing with a genuinely different mechanism: e.g. regime-conditional trailing (trail only in chop/old_thin where giveback bites, static in trends), a percent-of-MFE giveback stop rather than ATR-offset, or forward live giveback data. A flat ATR trail is closed.
post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: Trailing gave NO drawdown benefit (~11% either way), so it is strictly dominated by static here - it only sacrifices upside.
